From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-04-10T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Incident: Tokenization service degradation — 2027-04-10

Quick incident note: between 07:42 and 08:02 PT this morning our tokenization service (token-svc) experienced elevated error rates and slow responses for requests >1k tokens. We saw a sharp spike in CPU scheduler contention on the hosting pool after a background shard compaction job coincided with an unusually high continuous-batch window from a heavy customer workload.

Impact summary (prelim):
- Affected traffic: ~9% of total hosted text-generation requests (predominantly long-context customers).
- Customer-facing errors: ~0.9% of tokens returned as 5xx; transient timeouts for long requests.
- SLA: one customer (Acme Corp) reported degraded latency for a 30-minute window; we are investigating whether this qualifies as an SLA incident under their contract.

What we did:
- Immediate mitigation: paused compaction job (compaction-job-7), scaled an extra pool of dedicated tokenizer workers, and enabled a short-term routing split to reduce batch depth for long requests.
- Ongoing: collecting KV cache snapshots and logs, creating a draft postmortem.

Short ask: I have a postmortem draft attached (token-service-postmortem-draft.pdf). Leadership requested a one-page board-ready exec summary with OKR implications and a clear action register. Will circulate a board-ready summary by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: token-service-postmortem-draft.pdf (pdf, draft)

— Jonas
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-04-11T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Board-ready summary and action register — Token-svc incident (04/10)

Attached: board-summary-token-incident-20270411.pdf (board-ready PDF)

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- What happened: A background shard compaction job overlapped with an atypical continuous-batching window from a small set of long-context customers, causing scheduler contention in token-svc and increased latency/errors for long requests.
- Severity: Customer-facing degradation for ~20 minutes; estimated customer error rate spike of 0.9% across traffic during that window. Potential SLA exposure for Acme Corp for a 30-minute elevated latency window.
- Root cause (concise): insufficient isolation between maintenance compaction jobs and hot request routing; compaction increases CPU and memory pressure that pushes tokenization tasks behind scheduling deadlines under heavy batching.

Impact & Customers:
- Named affected customer: Acme Corporation — they reported elevated tail latency on a transactional integration. Their support ticket: HUB-ACME-4212 (link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/ACME-CORP).
- Platform metrics: average P95 latency for token-svc rose from 210ms -> 820ms for long requests during the window. Error (5xx) counts rose by ~8x for affected shards.

Immediate and near-term actions (owners + due dates):
1) Containment: disable compaction-job-7 during peak hours. Owner: Jonas Weber. Due: 2027-04-10 (done).
2) Capacity: provision and keep an extra tokenizer worker pool for 3 weeks, auto-scale policy tweak to limit batch depth for long requests. Owner: Marissa Cole (Infra). Due: 2027-04-13.
3) Routing: implement a routing rule to triage requests >1k tokens to a low-batching path. Owner: SRE + Runtime Team. Due: 2027-04-20.
4) Observability: add a scheduler contention metric and an automated alert when compaction overlaps with high batch depth. Owner: Jonas Weber. Due: 2027-04-18.
5) SLAs/Customer remediation: draft an incident credit calculation for Acme and prepare comms with Customer Success. Owner: Hannah Schmitt. Due: 2027-04-14.

Longer-term remediation (OKR alignment / roadmap impact):
- Workstream A (Runtime resiliency): prioritize a scheduled-jobs isolation feature in Q3 (estimated effort: 2 engineers, 2 quarters) — affects OKR infra.resilience.
- Workstream B (Batching controls): expose batch-depth controls for enterprise customers to set per-route. (1 eng, 1 quarter).

Concise risk to OKRs:
- Infra resiliency OKR: medium risk (priority move — 10% OKR score hit if not addressed by quarter end).
- Customer retention OKR for named accounts: low-to-medium risk until SLA remediation completed.

Customer comms: initial outreach done by CS; proposed credit offering in draft attached.

Attachments: board-summary-token-incident-20270411.pdf

Forwarding Jonas' board summary with a short product/roadmap lens.

Key points for OKR owners:
- Product metrics affected: retention signal for >1k token workflows dropped by ~2.3% in the day following the incident (users with repeated long-context queries).
- OKR exposure: Feature OKR "Improve long-context reliability" is at risk; if routing/batching controls are not expedited, we expect a ~6% negative delta on that OKR by EOW next quarter.

Proposed resource moves (decision requested):
- Shift 1 platform engineer from feature backlog to Runtime resiliency for 3 sprints (Apr–Jun). Estimated cost: ~0.4 FTE on feature delivery; benefits: reduces mean time to isolation for maintenance jobs and accelerates routing rule delivery.
- Approve expedited engineering budget for a temporary on-call SRE rotation to implement batch-depth routing (estimated one-time budget approval).
